units.function: Cross-surface parser and formatter regression tests for Codex JSONL session, usage, reasoning, command, file-change and error events.
units.dependencyDirection: One server test imports vendor-specific server, UI and CLI entry points from @paperclipai/adapter-codex-local; static JSONL fixtures are parsed directly with no runtime process, database, API, authorization or event persistence.
units.keyDataModels: Codex thread_id, item/turn lifecycle events, agent_message/reasoning/command_execution/file_change/error items, usage tokens and Paperclip stream-event/console projections.
units.lifecycle: Codex emits newline-delimited private events -> server parser derives session/summary/usage/error -> UI parser maps individual lines to display events -> CLI formatter prints selected raw fields.
units.testAssessment: All 6 focused tests passed with PAPERCLIP_HOME redirected to /tmp. They provide inexpensive fixture compatibility for several happy-path vendor events but do not test process execution, streaming boundaries, schema/version drift, malformed or oversized input, unknown events, cancellation, replay, truncation, redaction, persistence or authorization.
units.designRationale: Keep server result extraction and operator-facing UI/CLI projections aligned with Codex JSONL output and catch known stale-session and model-access failure shapes.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs each vendor Connector to translate private runtime protocols into one versioned, secret-free, idempotent progress/evidence/result contract without leaking vendor sessions or raw sensitive activity into the control plane.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT only as a raft/codex-specific Connector compatibility test pattern. Keep all Codex event names and parsing in the adapter package; map to neutral event codes, capability declarations, classified/truncated evidence references and opaque external session handles. The core must not import this package or depend on English errors.
units.responsibilityConflict: The tested projection exposes raw reasoning, shell commands, absolute paths, command output and vendor error text without binding them to work, principal, granted data/tool scope, approval digest or evidence retention policy. A session ID plus summary cannot establish the required responsibility chain.
evidence: 2026-08-19 focused Vitest with temporary PAPERCLIP_HOME: 6/6 passed
units.securityFindings: HIGH data-exposure concern: UI/CLI events include raw reasoning, full shell command lines, absolute local paths, aggregated stdout and upstream error messages, with no redaction/classification assertions. MEDIUM compatibility concern: tests encode vendor-private strings and event shapes but omit version negotiation and unknown-event behavior. Missing adversarial cases include secrets in argv/output/path/error, ANSI/control sequences, malformed or deeply nested JSON, huge lines/output, partial/multiline chunks, duplicate/out-of-order events, multiple Agent messages/turns, stale-session false positives and stable error-code mapping.
